name: Starvemaxxing

card.summary: Starvemaxxing is the looksmaxxing term for sharply cutting food intake, through fasting or very low calories, to get a leaner, more defined face and body quickly.
card.note: Prolonged severe restriction is associated with muscle loss and metabolic adaptation, and community members themselves caution strongly against it during puberty.

quick.overview:
Starvemaxxing means eating very little, or nothing for days, to lose body fat fast. The appearance goal is a leaner face with more visible bone structure, jawline and cheekbones, and a slimmer, more defined body.

Users describe it as a faster alternative to a slow 1,500-calorie cut, where progress can take months and one binge can feel like it erases a week. Physiology references describe the body drawing on glycogen, then fat, and eventually muscle protein during prolonged starvation, and community threads often warn about muscle loss, rebound eating and growth concerns for teenagers.
quick.how: Practitioners describe water fasts of several days, multi-day very-low-calorie stretches, or aggressive 24-hour-plus fasts, sometimes supported by appetite-suppressing medication that users mention by name in forum threads. The idea in these threads is to lose most of the weight in a short push, then switch to maintenance.
quick.risks: Severe restriction is linked in physiology references to loss of muscle mass and reduced energy expenditure. Forum members say it is especially unwise in puberty, when they argue growth needs plentiful food, and some report regretting it. Binge-restrict cycles and nutrient shortfalls are commonly raised concerns. Anyone with a history of disordered eating is generally advised by clinicians to seek professional support.

lead: Starvemaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for dramatic calorie restriction, usually extended fasting or very low intake, used to get lean quickly. The aim is a visibly leaner face, where lower facial fat can make the jaw, cheekbones and eye area look more defined, and a slimmer body overall.[1][2]

Users of looksmax.org describe it as a response to the slowness of ordinary cutting: one poster said a 1,500-calorie diet left them hungry, took months to move the scale and could be undone by a single binge, and argued for losing the weight in about a month and then maintaining.[2] Others in the same thread recommend higher intake plus cardio instead.[2]

Physiology references describe the body burning stored glycogen first, then fat, and breaking down muscle protein in prolonged starvation, along with a reduction in metabolic rate.[4] Community threads also include warnings from members about starving during puberty.[3]

chain: Rapid fat loss across face and body
Sharper jaw, cheekbones and a leaner look
angle.text: Lower body fat makes underlying bone structure and muscle outline more visible, so people use short, aggressive restriction to reach a lean look quickly. Practitioners usually follow it with a maintenance phase.

infobox: Divided; strong warnings about use in teens

paras: The term combines starve with the looksmaxxing suffix -maxxing. It refers to deliberate severe restriction for appearance, as opposed to moderate calorie deficits or time-restricted eating. Forum threads title it as a question of effectiveness, safety and method.[1][2]

Posters list water fasting and extended no-food periods among methods. In a 2020s thread a user said that on a GLP-1-type appetite suppressant they could go over 24 hours without eating on a single pastry; this illustrates how some pair restriction with medication.[1]

Proponents argue that fast loss is easier mentally than a long, slow cut and avoids hours of cardio, and that a short intense phase followed by maintenance gets the desired facial and body leanness sooner.[2]
Opponents within the same communities say moderate deficits with more activity are better, and that restriction during growth is harmful.[2][3]

General physiology references describe starvation as depleting glycogen, then fat, then breaking down muscle protein, and a metabolic adaptation that lowers energy expenditure.[4] Such references describe adult responses; none address looks outcomes of deliberate starvemaxxing.

Members of looksmax.org write that starving at 15 to 17 is dangerous and one says they believe they would be a few centimetres taller without it; another says puberty is a time to eat generously from quality sources.[3] Prolonged restriction is also described as risking muscle loss and rebound binges.[2][4]

lore.intro: Starvemaxxing is discussed across many looksmax.org threads, with posters asking about methods, effectiveness and age safety.[1][2][3]

claims.claim: Starving for a short period is the fastest way to a leaner face
claims.believers: Posters say slow 1,500-calorie cuts take months and are derailed by binges, so a short severe phase then maintenance is preferable.[2]
claims.experts: Physiology references describe fat loss alongside muscle breakdown and lowered energy expenditure in prolonged starvation; looks outcomes have not been studied.[4]

claims.claim: Appetite-suppressing drugs make multi-day fasting easy
claims.believers: A poster said that on a GLP-1-type drug they ate a single 500-calorie item and went over 24 hours without eating.[1]
claims.experts: No published study has examined this use for appearance.

claims.claim: Starvemaxxing during puberty can harm growth
claims.believers: Teenagers' threads include replies saying it cost them height and that puberty is for eating generously.[3]
claims.experts: Adolescent growth is not covered by the starvation physiology references consulted; clinicians generally describe adequate nutrition as needed for growth.
